headline: A Bank of Japan deputy governor says the AI boom may change the level at which interest rates eventually settle.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a central bank deputy governor says AI may raise the level where interest rates settle, with Japanese bond yields near three-decade highs.
importance_line: Borrowers and savers in Japan and bond investors elsewhere may face higher rates for longer if AI lifts the neutral rate, though Uchida described possibilities rather than a decision.
summary: Business Insider reports that Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida said in a Tokyo speech on Monday that AI is a "big positive demand shock" and could change the neutral rate of interest, the level that neither stimulates nor restrains the economy. If that rate is rising, central banks may need to keep policy rates higher than investors expect, and Japan's 10-year government bond yield stood near 3.09% that day, close to a three-decade high.
notes: Same speech as C07-04. Business Insider also cites ING strategists (last week) saying AI could account for roughly one-fifth of the recent rise in long-term bond yields.
